request.message: I am turning left at a junction while an oncoming car goes straight ahead. In another situation I turn right across a pavement with a cyclist approaching. Who must I yield to in each case, and which numbered parts of section 7 apply?

response.reply:
In the first case you must yield to the oncoming car; in the second you must yield to the cyclist on the pavement. The first is Trafikkreglene § 7 no. 2, the second is § 7 no. 3.

Left turn across oncoming traffic: when you swing left, the oncoming car ends up on your right side, and that is exactly what creates your duty to give way. You are the servant here and the oncoming car is the king — it should not have to brake or hesitate because of you. Going straight does not by itself hand anyone priority; what matters is that you are the one crossing its path. Slow down early and let it pass before you commit.

Right turn across a pavement: when you turn and cross a pavement, you must give way to pedestrians, cyclists and small electric vehicles on that pavement. The cyclist is going straight along their path, you are the one cutting across it, so the cyclist goes first. Check your mirror and blind spot before the turn — a quarter of a second is all it takes.

One thing worth keeping straight: giving way is not the same as always stopping. It means slowing down in good time so the other person never has to think about you. You stop only when that is the only way to avoid hindering them — or when a stop sign demands a full stop regardless.

And the general duty underneath both situations sits in § 7 no. 1: do not hinder or disturb the road user you are giving way to, and make your intention clear by adjusting speed early.
